evals.query: We're adding a 'Reply for me' button to the support inbox in our help desk tool for small online shops. One click and the AI reads the conversation and sends a reply to the customer. Leadership wants it in four weeks. Design how it should work.
expected_behavior: Changes the flow so nothing reaches the customer until the support agent has seen and approved the draft (or argues for narrow exceptions with safeguards).
Makes the button label match what it does (for example 'Draft reply' if it drafts).
Grounds replies in the shop's own information (orders, policies) and shows the agent what the draft is based on, flagging when it is unsure.
Designs the waiting and failure states honestly (progress while drafting, what happens on an error, never a silent empty draft).
Defines how quality will be judged before launch: a set of real past conversations, criteria, and a pass bar that must be met to ship.
Addresses customer data (what is sent to the model and kept) and lets agents edit and report bad drafts.

evals.query: Leadership wants to ship AI meeting summaries in our notes app next week. I reviewed 20 sample summaries against the recordings; my notes are attached. Is it ready?
expected_behavior: Gives a direct answer first: ready or not, and on what condition.
Counts the problems in the notes and separates the serious ones (two invented action items, one wrong owner, one missed decision) from the minor ones, with rates (for example 4 serious in 20).

Points out that 20 short internal meetings with good audio is too small and narrow a sample, and names conditions not tested (for example long meetings, crosstalk, poor audio, customers' meetings, other languages).
Proposes a pass bar and an evaluation set that would make the answer yes.
Proposes product safeguards for the errors that will remain (for example labelling as AI-generated, linking each action item to the moment in the recording, review before sharing).
Does not overstate certainty from 20 samples.
